claims.assertion: The trip deviated far beyond tolerance: 9.6 km driven against a 3.9 km optimal route, +5.7 km (+144%), well over the 1 km threshold in RD-1, so a refund is owed.

The first off-route segment (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) is covered by the rider's consent: the driver asked 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' at 14:01 and the rider answered 'Okay, sure, go ahead' at 14:02, and CAVENAGH ROAD is among that segment's roads driven.

The rider's only added request was 'Can you stop at a 711 on the way? I need to grab something quick one.' — an unspecified 7-Eleven somewhere along the way, with no named road or place; it does not authorise a 2.87 km detour out to Beach Road.

The second off-route segment (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, 1,553 m off the optimal route, via BEACH ROAD) was not consented to in advance: the driver's Beach Road choice appears only in his post-trip statement, and no rider message before 14:17:45 names Beach Road or any place on that segment.

The stop the driver made was at (1.3025, 103.8638), 2,995 m from pickup and 2,098 m from drop-off — not a pickup/drop-off point and not 'on the way'; the 4 min 10 s stationary there is a stop of the driver's own choosing under RD-3.

The driver's traffic justification covers only the replaced Orchard Road stretch (accident at 13:52, Orchard Road band 1 during 14:00–14:10), which the rider's Cavenagh agreement already covers; Bras Basah Road (band 4) and Bayfront Avenue (band 3) were free-flowing during the trip, so there is no traffic reason for the 14:17–14:29 loop out to Beach Road and back under RD-4.

The deviation segment was not exempt, and it had no traffic reason, so the excess distance fare of $7.99 (5.67 km × $1.4100/km, this trip's distance fare ÷ distance) is refundable, less nothing for the consented Cavenagh detour since that part was agreed.

Because no traffic reason excuses the unconsented Beach Road segment, a driver violation should be recorded against the driver; the rider, by contrast, has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days on a 610-day, 4.9-rated account, while the driver has 3 disputes and 1 upheld in 90 days.

The driver's written statement says the rider sent a voice note agreeing to Cavenagh and asked for a stop, but the only pre-segment rider agreement in the record is the text message at 14:02 answering the Cavenagh question; the driver's word alone about a voice note is a claim, not consent, and no in-app call recording appears in the record.

Since only chat notice of a reroute without a pre-agreed road is in issue and the rider was not informed before or at the point of the Beach Road deviation, the driver should at least receive a notification-duty reminder logged on his route compliance record.

weaknesses: The rider's own message F10 asks to 'stop at a 711 on the way' and the driver did stop at a 7-Eleven (F2 stationary 14:20–14:24, F13 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road'), so the driver will argue RD-3 exempts the whole 14:17–14:29 segment rather than only a reasonable short stop.
